issue_paraphrase: When a query result set contains two columns with the same name, as happens naturally in joins, and the connection uses the namedtuple row factory, the factory lets a plain Python ValueError from the standard library escape instead of raising a psycopg exception, so user code that catches psycopg errors does not see it. Duplicate column names should surface as a psycopg DataError like the other data-shape errors.
fix_summary: rows._make_nt now wraps the collections.namedtuple() call in try/except ValueError and re-raises as psycopg.exceptions.DataError (from None), so the non-psycopg exception no longer leaks out of the row factory.
notes: No PostgreSQL server needed: the regression test calls the private rows._make_nt() directly (as upstream does). Whole file tests/test_rows.py collects and the single test runs in ~0.05s at 1 CPU. conftest.py pytest_plugins force-import psycopg_pool at pytest startup, so psycopg_pool must be installed too or every test errors at collection. issue_paraphrase: On platforms where psycopg falls back to the generic selector-based wait function, any operation that needs two consecutive waits on the same connection - for example a connect that first waits for the socket to become writable and is then woken and waits again for it to become readable - dies with an unexpected KeyError about the file descriptor already being registered. The wait loop keeps re-registering the same descriptor instead of updating its registration, so multi-phase operations crash instead of completing.
fix_summary: wait_selector now remembers the last registration mask (last_s) and, after being woken, only calls sel.unregister()+sel.register() when the generator's new wait state differs from the current one; the fd registration is no longer overwritten while still active.
notes: No PostgreSQL server needed: the included direct repro uses a socketpair and a fake two-phase generator; the upstream test test_wait_r uses only localhost sockets (marked slow; the wait_selector slice of 16 tests runs in ~18s at 1 CPU, the interval=2 combos take ~2-4s each). Run pytest from the repo root. The regression test (commit 5369bbc9) is a later commit than the fix: at parent_commit the in-tree test file still had the old single-event form, so the parent-direction run must check out tests/test_waiting.py and tests/test_waiting_async.py from 5369bbc9 (as recorded in reproduction); at the fix commit the code passes with those test files. Discriminating combos are the four nevents=2 / ready=R parametrizations (ids listed in golden_test_names); the ready=NONE combos pass at both ends.

issue_paraphrase: Passing a client_encoding option in the connection string that uses any of PostgreSQL's documented charset alias names - such as MSKANJI, which is the PostgreSQL name for Shift_JIS - makes psycopg silently ignore the requested encoding and fall back to utf-8. Server text is then decoded with the wrong codec and comes out corrupted. All the PostgreSQL alias names from the documented charset table should resolve to the matching Python codec.
fix_summary: _encodings.py was restructured from a flat name->codec dict to a table keyed by tuples of (canonical name, documented aliases) per PostgreSQL charset; the runtime py_codecs mapping is built by upper-casing and stripping '-'/'_' (plus a no-underscore variant), so aliases like MSKANJI, Mskanji, ShiftJIS, WIN932, UHC, WIN949, ALT, ABC resolve e.g. to shift_jis, cp949, cp866, cp1258.
notes: No PostgreSQL server needed; the function under test parses the conninfo string only. The whole test_conninfo_encoding parametrization (9 rows) runs in ~0.05s at 1 CPU. Discriminating rows are the MSKANJI/mskanji ones; the Unicode/UNICODE rows return utf-8 at both ends (canonical UTF8 also maps to utf-8). Run pytest from the repo root (non-editable install) and python repros from a cwd other than the repo root, as for the other entries.
